candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to d_resid4. Record rho, rho_abs, exact within-Ser p, exact sixfold-family p, and global matched-support p. This candidate is only an auditable route, not a verdict, unless it passes coverage, residual-norm, independence, and projection gates.
candidate_axes.construction: For each mature tRNA, discard anticodon bases 34, 35, 36 and discard any feature explicitly annotated as wobble-position decoding. Encode only non-wobble modification features at positions 32, 37, 38 and body positions: binary presence, chemistry class counts, enzyme-family counts, and evidence-weighted modification burden. Within each organism, z-score each feature across tRNA isodecoders, map tRNAs to their directly cognate standard-code codons, aggregate multiple isodecoders per codon by median, then aggregate organisms by median to obtain a 61-vector x. Residualize x against the locked forbidden matrix C containing intercept, amino-acid one-hot, tRNA supply/tAI, tRNA consensus loading, f3/ramp, d_perp, optimal_loading, GC1/GC2/GC3/total_GC, wobble class, codon-pair incoming/outgoing scores, mRNA-stability score, and ribosome-dwell score. If r=(I-P_C)x is nonzero, set d_resid4=r/||r||_2.
controls: Position-34, anticodon-base, and wobble-decoding features are excluded before modeling.
Gene-copy number, tAI, and any expression-derived tRNA abundance column are controls only, never inputs to x.

Reject the axis if residual x is predictable from tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble class, codon-pair scores, mRNA stability, or ribosome dwell at preregistered adjusted R2 >= 0.05 in held-out organisms.
Run leave-one-organism and leave-one-enzyme-family audits; the sign and material SerSplit projection must not depend on a single clade or a single modification enzyme.
Negative controls: repeat with permuted modification positions within each tRNA body and with anticodon labels permuted within isotype; both must lose the SerSplit projection.
data_sources: MODOMICS tRNA modification table: organism, tRNA isotype, anticodon, mature-position number, modification identity, enzyme, evidence type
GtRNAdb 2.0 or tRNADB-CE tRNA records for the locked organism panel: organism, tRNA gene ID, isotype, anticodon, predicted mature sequence, isodecoder family
standard-code 61-sense-codon table and locked codon order from the local selection-vector packet
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if non-wobble modification coverage is sparse for Ser UCN or AGY codons, if residualization removes nearly all variance, if the result is driven by tRNA abundance or anticodon/wobble annotations, or if SerSplit projection is not stable under leave-one-source audits.
candidate_axes.name: non_wobble_tRNA_modification_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residualized kinetic axis. Also run an assay-source split: public-only versus fill-in-only projections must have the same nonzero sign after the sign convention is locked by the training half.
candidate_axes.construction: Use only wild-type, full-length, cognate aminoacylation assays. Exclude assays where the measured substrate is an anticodon mutant, minihelix-only substrate, noncognate mischarging substrate, or abundance proxy. Convert kcat/Km to log10 units; within each organism-aaRS-assay-method block, subtract the amino-acid-specific median and divide by MAD. Map each tRNA substrate to decoded standard codon; aggregate technical replicates by inverse-variance weighted mean, isodecoders by median, and organisms by random-effects meta-analytic mean to obtain x over 61 codons. Residualize x against C and define d_resid4=r/||r||_2 if ||r||_2 is above the locked tolerance.
controls: Amino-acid one-hot is included in C, so any amino-acid-level Ser effect is removed before testing the Ser UCN versus AGY split.
Anticodon-mutation assays are excluded, preventing an anticodon/wobble mechanism from becoming the raw axis.
Assay batch, organism, temperature, pH, and method are normalized before codon aggregation.
tRNA supply, tRNA consensus, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-dwell controls are residualized after aggregation.
Coverage gate: every sense codon must have direct or preregistered fill-in kinetic support; otherwise the candidate remains incomplete.
data_sources: BRENDA and SABIO-RK aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase assay records: enzyme, organism, tRNA substrate, amino acid, kcat, Km, kcat/Km, temperature, pH, buffer, assay method
manual primary-literature extraction table for full-length cognate tRNA aminoacylation kinetics
bounded fill-in experiment if public coverage is incomplete: purified cognate mature tRNA panel with at least one directly assigned tRNA substrate for each of the 61 sense codons
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if fewer than 61 codons have direct kinetic values, if Ser codon values are inferred only from anticodon identity, if organism or assay-method effects dominate, or if the SerSplit projection disappears after amino-acid and tRNA controls.
candidate_axes.name: aaRS_aminoacylation_kinetics_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the EF-Tu/EF1A residual axis. Projection is interpreted only as a candidate-axis hit if the same sign appears in at least two independent assay sources or in one public source plus the bounded fill-in panel.
candidate_axes.construction: For each charged tRNA substrate, compute deltaG=RT ln(Kd) or use reported deltaG. Within each organism and elongation-factor assay block, subtract the amino-acid median to remove amino-acid-side-chain binding compensation. Exclude uncharged tRNA, minihelix, anticodon-mutant, and wobble-only constructs. Map charged tRNAs to codons by direct cognate assignment; aggregate isodecoders and organisms as robust medians to form x. Residualize x against C and normalize the residual to d_resid4.
controls: The raw score is binding thermodynamics of charged tRNA, not tRNA abundance, codon usage, or ribosome dwell.
Amino-acid one-hot, tRNA supply, tRNA consensus, wobble class, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-dwell scores are controls.
Reject if binding values correlate with tAI or gene copy after residualization.
Run charged-versus-uncharged exclusion audit: uncharged-tRNA controls must not produce the same SerSplit projection.
Run buffer/method leave-one-out audits.
data_sources: published EF-Tu or EF1A aminoacyl-tRNA binding datasets with Kd, kon, koff, or deltaG for charged full-length tRNAs
tRNA substrate metadata: organism, amino acid, anticodon, mature sequence, charging enzyme, modification state
bounded fill-in binding panel: one purified charged mature tRNA per sense codon, same EF-Tu/EF1A preparation and buffer
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if full 61-codon charged-tRNA coverage cannot be obtained, if Ser UCN or AGY values are inferred from shared amino-acid effects, if EF-Tu affinity is collinear with tRNA consensus loading, or if the projection is assay-batch-specific.
candidate_axes.name: EF_Tu_charged_tRNA_binding_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the lability residual axis. Report whether the projection survives the exclusion of events annotated as tRNA-loss, wobble-driven, GC-driven, or codon-disappearance-driven.
candidate_axes.construction: For each standard-code sense codon, count phylogenetically deduplicated independent reassignment or ambiguous-assignment events in which that codon changes amino-acid meaning or becomes stop. Exclude events whose only support is tRNA abundance loss, codon disappearance, or wobble expansion unless an independent genomic/translation assignment is present. Normalize as x_i=log((events_i+0.5)/(opportunities_i-events_i+0.5)), where opportunities are the number of screened independent clades in which the codon was observable. Residualize x against C plus codon-family degeneracy and stop-adjacency indicators; normalize the residual to d_resid4 if nonzero.
controls: Phylogenetic deduplication prevents one clade expansion from counting as many events.
GC, codon disappearance, tRNA loss/supply, wobble class, codon-pair effects, mRNA stability, and ribosome dwell are controls or exclusion reasons, not explanatory inputs.
Remove all stop codons from the tested 61-vector; stop-adjacency is a control only.
Repeat after excluding mitochondrial codes and after excluding bacterial/archaeal candidate recodings; projection must not be unique to one domain.
Negative control: randomize reassignment events across codons within equal degeneracy classes and recompute the projection.
data_sources: NCBI Genetic Codes table snapshot: code ID, taxon scope, codon assignment, evidence note
Codetta or equivalent alternative-code screen calls on GTDB representative genomes: genome ID, codon reassignment, confidence, clade, inferred mechanism if annotated
GTDB or NCBI taxonomy tree for phylogenetic deduplication of reassignment events
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if reassignment counts are too sparse, if SerSplit signal is fully explained by alternative-code mechanisms involving tRNA supply or wobble, if AGY/UCN differences are driven by stop-adjacent recoding artifacts, or if residualization collapses the axis.
candidate_axes.name: codon_assignment_lability_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual mutability axis after all DNA-context controls. Also report rho after removing CpG-containing codons and after matching UCN and AGY codons by genome-wide opportunity where possible.
candidate_axes.construction: For each sense codon, compute an opportunity-normalized synonymous mutation burden: observed rare synonymous SNVs from that codon divided by callable occurrences of that codon, stratified by strand, methylated-CpG status, local trinucleotide context, replication timing if available, and gene constraint. Use only variants classified as synonymous in the locked transcript set; exclude codon changes affecting splice motifs or overlapping regulatory annotations. Fit a neutral-context model from noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites, subtract expected mutation burden, and aggregate the residual by codon to x. Residualize x against C plus explicit CpG/UpA and local trinucleotide mutability columns; normalize to d_resid4.
controls: The raw axis is DNA damage/repair or mutability residual, not translation efficiency, tRNA supply, ribosome dwell, mRNA stability, or codon-pair usage.
GC1/GC2/GC3/total_GC, CpG, TpA/UpA, methylation, trinucleotide mutation opportunity, codon-pair scores, mRNA-stability scores, and dwell scores are controls.
Exclude disease-enriched, splice-proximal, nonsense-adjacent, and overlapping functional elements.
Repeat in separate ancestry groups and in de novo-only data; the candidate is rejected if projection exists only in one ascertainment source.
Negative control: use intronic pseudo-codons in the same genes and reading-frame phases; they must not reproduce the SerSplit projection.
data_sources: gnomAD or comparable population coding SNV table: variant, allele count, allele number, gene, transcript, codon position, ancestral/ref/alt allele, consequence
de novo mutation or near-neutral pedigree mutation table with callable opportunity mask
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon, reading frame, exon, strand
COSMIC/PCAWG mutational-signature exposure table only as a control source, not as the raw axis
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if GC/CpG/trinucleotide context explains the residual, if coding selection or splice/regulatory overlap drives the score, if the 61-codon opportunity table is incomplete, or if SerSplit projection is absent in de novo mutation data.
candidate_axes.name: synonymous_DNA_damage_repair_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the editing residual axis. Report projections separately for A-to-I-only, C-to-U-only, and combined axes; only preregistered combined or replicated type-specific projections are considered candidate hits.
candidate_axes.construction: Map high-confidence RNA editing sites into CDS codons. For each sense codon, compute editing burden per callable expressed codon occurrence, separately for A-to-I and C-to-U, requiring minimum read depth and excluding known DNA variants. Normalize within tissue by expression, coverage, editable-base opportunity, and local sequence motif; combine tissues by median or random-effects meta-analysis to produce x. Residualize x against C plus expression, editable-base count, ADAR/APOBEC motif score, RBP density, and mRNA half-life; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: DNA SNPs and mapping-ambiguous sites are excluded.
mRNA stability, expression, coverage, local editing motif, GC, codon-pair, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, wobble, and ribosome dwell are residualized or matched.
Run tissue leave-one-out and editing-type-specific audits.
Negative control: shift CDS reading frame by +1 and +2 before codon aggregation; shifted pseudo-codons must not reproduce the projection.
Reject if SerSplit projection is driven by a single tissue, transcript family, or editable-base composition.
data_sources: REDIportal, RADAR, or equivalent A-to-I and C-to-U RNA editing calls: genomic coordinate, transcript, editing type, editing level, coverage, tissue, strand
GTEx or ENCODE RNA-seq coverage/expression table for opportunity normalization
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation with codon coordinate and reading frame
mRNA half-life and RNA-binding-protein annotation tracks used only as controls
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if RNA editing burden is explained by editable-base composition, expression, mRNA half-life, local motifs, or mapping artifacts, or if coverage is insufficient for all 61 sense codons.
candidate_axes.name: coding_RNA_editing_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to each preregistered modification-type residual and to the combined residual after Holm correction over modification types. No biological-axis claim is made from a single unreplicated modification source.
candidate_axes.construction: Map mRNA modification calls inside coding regions to codon identity and codon position. For each sense codon, compute opportunity-normalized modification burden per expressed codon occurrence, stratified by modification type and codon position. Normalize within study and tissue by expression, coverage, modification-calling platform, local motif score, and codon-position opportunity; aggregate across studies by robust median to obtain x. Residualize x against C plus mRNA half-life, predicted local structure, RBP motif density, and known modification motifs; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: mRNA stability and local RNA structure are controls, not the candidate axis.
GC, motif content, codon-pair score, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, wobble, and ribosome dwell are residualized.
Run platform-specific audits: antibody-based, nanopore/direct-RNA, and chemical-mapping calls are tested separately where available.
Negative control: use UTR modification calls randomly assigned to CDS codons by expression-matched transcript; projection must vanish.
Reject modification types with fewer than a preregistered minimum number of codon-mapped events.
data_sources: RMBase, m6A-Atlas, DirectRMDB, or equivalent transcriptome modification calls: modification type, coordinate, transcript, tissue/cell type, confidence, stoichiometry if available
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon coordinate, reading frame
matched expression, mRNA half-life, local motif, and structure tracks used as controls
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if modification calls are motif/GC/stability artifacts, if platform bias dominates, if events are too sparse for 61 codons, or if SerSplit projection is not replicated across independent mapping technologies.
candidate_axes.name: mRNA_base_modification_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the MAVE residual codon-effect axis. Report public-only, assay-type-specific, and leave-one-gene projections; the route remains exploratory unless projection is stable across independent assays.
candidate_axes.construction: Extract only synonymous single-codon substitutions from multiplexed assays. Convert each variant score to an effect of using the alternate codon relative to the reference codon within the same amino acid and local protein position. Fit a mixed model with random intercepts for gene, assay, protein position, amino acid, source codon, target codon, and replicate; take the best linear unbiased codon-use effect for each of the 61 codons as x. Residualize x against C plus assay-specific RNA-structure, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and dwell covariates; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: Only synonymous substitutions are used; nonsynonymous and splice/regulatory variants are excluded.
Amino-acid identity, gene, protein position, assay, source codon, target codon, expression, codon-pair, mRNA stability, ribosome dwell, GC, wobble, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, and d_perp are controlled.
Leave-one-gene-family and leave-one-assay-type audits are required.
Negative control: permute synonymous scores within amino acid and gene while preserving codon counts; projection must vanish.
Reject if SerSplit projection is carried by one gene, one assay, or one codon substitution direction.
data_sources: MaveDB and ProteinGym synonymous variant tables: variant sequence, reference codon, alternate codon, score, raw counts, replicate ID, assay type, selection condition
gene/transcript annotation for each MAVE library: CDS position, amino acid, codon context, expression construct, library design
matched codon-pair, RNA-structure, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-profiling controls for each assayed gene where available
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if MAVE coverage does not span all 61 codons, if effects are dominated by mRNA stability/codon-pair/dwell terms, if synonymous scores are too assay-specific, or if the model cannot identify codon effects separately from gene and position effects.
candidate_axes.name: synonymous_MAVE_effect_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT separately to each lesion chemistry and to any preregistered combined lesion axis. Report whether projection survives explicit GC and nearest-neighbor residualization.
candidate_axes.construction: Synthesize oligos in which only the central codon varies across the 61 sense codons and all flanking bases, concentration, exposure, time, temperature, and buffer are identical. For each damage chemistry, estimate lesion rate per molecule from raw replicate counts. Within chemistry and replicate batch, z-score lesion rates; aggregate independent chemistries only if preregistered or keep separate axes. The raw codon lesion vector x is then residualized against C plus explicit base-composition, purine/pyrimidine, CpG/UpA, and nearest-neighbor thermodynamic controls; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: No tRNA, codon usage, mRNA stability, codon-pair, ribosome, or expression data enter the raw axis.
Identical flanking contexts remove codon-pair and local transcript-context effects at the experimental design stage.
GC, nearest-neighbor chemistry, CpG/UpA, and base-position composition are residualized.
Run DNA-only and RNA-only panels separately; projection must not depend on a single chemistry unless that chemistry was preregistered.
Negative control: replicate the panel with scrambled codon labels before analysis; projection must vanish.
data_sources: bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic DNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon
bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic RNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon
LC-MS, primer-extension, nanopore, or sequencing readouts for UV dimerization, oxidative lesions, hydrolytic deamination, and alkylation under fixed exposure conditions
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if lesion-rate differences are fully explained by GC/base composition or nearest-neighbor chemistry, if replicate variance is too high, if synthesis bias differs by codon, or if no residual projection onto u_SerSplit remains.
candidate_axes.name: matched_trinucleotide_chemical_lesion_residual_axis

Forbidden-control table C_base for the same 61 codons: intercept, 20 amino-acid one-hot columns, GC1, GC2, GC3, total_GC, CpG, UpA, purine/pyrimidine position indicators, wobble class, codon-family degeneracy, and any local graph covariates already used in the Window6--Codon-Q6 bridge.

Codon-pair control table: for each codon, incoming codon-pair residual score, outgoing codon-pair residual score, source organism, transcript set, normalization method, and whether stop-adjacent pairs were excluded.

mRNA-stability control table: per-codon matched-context predicted deltaG or stability contribution, source transcriptome, window size, folding software/version, expression weighting, and GC-controlled residual.

ribosome-dwell control table: per-codon dwell or pause residual from matched ribosome-profiling sources, source organism, protocol, footprint length handling, A/P/E-site assignment, expression threshold, and existing tRNA/GC/stability residualization status.

For tRNA-modification route: MODOMICS/GtRNAdb/tRNADB-CE joined table with organism, tRNA ID, isotype, anticodon, decoded codon set, mature sequence, modification position, modification identity, enzyme, evidence, and abundance/gene-copy columns marked as controls only.

For EF-Tu/EF1A route: binding table with organism, elongation factor, charged tRNA substrate ID, amino acid, anticodon, decoded codon, Kd or deltaG, kon, koff if available, buffer, temperature, replicate, modification state, and source.

For alternative-code route: codon reassignment event table with codon, standard assignment, observed assignment, taxon/clade, genome IDs, evidence type, confidence, inferred mechanism, GC content, codon disappearance score, tRNA-loss annotation, and phylogenetic deduplication ID.

For DNA mutability route: codon opportunity table, coding SNV table, de novo mutation table, methylation/CpG flags, local trinucleotide context, callable bases, transcript annotation, and filters for splice/regulatory overlap.

For RNA editing and mRNA modification routes: CDS-mapped event calls with transcript, coordinate, codon, codon position, event type, confidence, coverage, expression, tissue/cell type, platform, known DNA-variant exclusion, local motif, and mRNA half-life control.

For MAVE route: synonymous variant score table with raw counts, normalized scores, replicate IDs, reference codon, alternate codon, amino acid, gene, protein position, assay type, library design, and RNA/codon-context annotations.

For synthetic lesion route: raw replicate count matrix for 61 matched-flank DNA/RNA oligos, synthesis QC, concentration, exposure condition, chemistry, readout method, batch, and codon label key stored separately until after QC.

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual mutability axis after all DNA-context controls. Also report rho after removing CpG-containing codons and after matching UCN and AGY codons by genome-wide opportunity where possible.
candidate_axes.construction: For each sense codon, compute an opportunity-normalized synonymous mutation burden: observed rare synonymous SNVs from that codon divided by callable occurrences of that codon, stratified by strand, methylated-CpG status, local trinucleotide context, replication timing if available, and gene constraint. Use only variants classified as synonymous in the locked transcript set; exclude codon changes affecting splice motifs or overlapping regulatory annotations. Fit a neutral-context model from noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites, subtract expected mutation burden, and aggregate the residual by codon to x. Residualize x against C plus explicit CpG/UpA and local trinucleotide mutability columns; normalize to d_resid4.
controls: The raw axis is DNA damage/repair or mutability residual, not translation efficiency, tRNA supply, ribosome dwell, mRNA stability, or codon-pair usage.
GC1/GC2/GC3/total_GC, CpG, TpA/UpA, methylation, trinucleotide mutation opportunity, codon-pair scores, mRNA-stability scores, and dwell scores are controls.
Exclude disease-enriched, splice-proximal, nonsense-adjacent, and overlapping functional elements.
Repeat in separate ancestry groups and in de novo-only data; the candidate is rejected if projection exists only in one ascertainment source.
Negative control: use intronic pseudo-codons in the same genes and reading-frame phases; they must not reproduce the SerSplit projection.
data_sources: gnomAD or comparable population coding SNV table: variant, allele count, allele number, gene, transcript, codon position, ancestral/ref/alt allele, consequence
de novo mutation or near-neutral pedigree mutation table with callable opportunity mask
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon, reading frame, exon, strand
COSMIC/PCAWG mutational-signature exposure table only as a control source, not as the raw axis
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if GC/CpG/trinucleotide context explains the residual, if coding selection or splice/regulatory overlap drives the score, if the 61-codon opportunity table is incomplete, or if SerSplit projection is absent in de novo mutation data.
candidate_axes.name: synonymous_DNA_damage_repair_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the editing residual axis. Report projections separately for A-to-I-only, C-to-U-only, and combined axes; only preregistered combined or replicated type-specific projections are considered candidate hits.
candidate_axes.construction: Map high-confidence RNA editing sites into CDS codons. For each sense codon, compute editing burden per callable expressed codon occurrence, separately for A-to-I and C-to-U, requiring minimum read depth and excluding known DNA variants. Normalize within tissue by expression, coverage, editable-base opportunity, and local sequence motif; combine tissues by median or random-effects meta-analysis to produce x. Residualize x against C plus expression, editable-base count, ADAR/APOBEC motif score, RBP density, and mRNA half-life; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: DNA SNPs and mapping-ambiguous sites are excluded.
mRNA stability, expression, coverage, local editing motif, GC, codon-pair, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, wobble, and ribosome dwell are residualized or matched.
Run tissue leave-one-out and editing-type-specific audits.
Negative control: shift CDS reading frame by +1 and +2 before codon aggregation; shifted pseudo-codons must not reproduce the projection.
Reject if SerSplit projection is driven by a single tissue, transcript family, or editable-base composition.
data_sources: REDIportal, RADAR, or equivalent A-to-I and C-to-U RNA editing calls: genomic coordinate, transcript, editing type, editing level, coverage, tissue, strand
GTEx or ENCODE RNA-seq coverage/expression table for opportunity normalization
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation with codon coordinate and reading frame
mRNA half-life and RNA-binding-protein annotation tracks used only as controls
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if RNA editing burden is explained by editable-base composition, expression, mRNA half-life, local motifs, or mapping artifacts, or if coverage is insufficient for all 61 sense codons.
candidate_axes.name: coding_RNA_editing_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to each preregistered modification-type residual and to the combined residual after Holm correction over modification types. No biological-axis claim is made from a single unreplicated modification source.
candidate_axes.construction: Map mRNA modification calls inside coding regions to codon identity and codon position. For each sense codon, compute opportunity-normalized modification burden per expressed codon occurrence, stratified by modification type and codon position. Normalize within study and tissue by expression, coverage, modification-calling platform, local motif score, and codon-position opportunity; aggregate across studies by robust median to obtain x. Residualize x against C plus mRNA half-life, predicted local structure, RBP motif density, and known modification motifs; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: mRNA stability and local RNA structure are controls, not the candidate axis.
GC, motif content, codon-pair score, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, wobble, and ribosome dwell are residualized.
Run platform-specific audits: antibody-based, nanopore/direct-RNA, and chemical-mapping calls are tested separately where available.
Negative control: use UTR modification calls randomly assigned to CDS codons by expression-matched transcript; projection must vanish.
Reject modification types with fewer than a preregistered minimum number of codon-mapped events.
data_sources: RMBase, m6A-Atlas, DirectRMDB, or equivalent transcriptome modification calls: modification type, coordinate, transcript, tissue/cell type, confidence, stoichiometry if available
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon coordinate, reading frame
matched expression, mRNA half-life, local motif, and structure tracks used as controls
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if modification calls are motif/GC/stability artifacts, if platform bias dominates, if events are too sparse for 61 codons, or if SerSplit projection is not replicated across independent mapping technologies.
candidate_axes.name: mRNA_base_modification_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the MAVE residual codon-effect axis. Report public-only, assay-type-specific, and leave-one-gene projections; the route remains exploratory unless projection is stable across independent assays.
candidate_axes.construction: Extract only synonymous single-codon substitutions from multiplexed assays. Convert each variant score to an effect of using the alternate codon relative to the reference codon within the same amino acid and local protein position. Fit a mixed model with random intercepts for gene, assay, protein position, amino acid, source codon, target codon, and replicate; take the best linear unbiased codon-use effect for each of the 61 codons as x. Residualize x against C plus assay-specific RNA-structure, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and dwell covariates; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: Only synonymous substitutions are used; nonsynonymous and splice/regulatory variants are excluded.
Amino-acid identity, gene, protein position, assay, source codon, target codon, expression, codon-pair, mRNA stability, ribosome dwell, GC, wobble, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, and d_perp are controlled.
Leave-one-gene-family and leave-one-assay-type audits are required.
Negative control: permute synonymous scores within amino acid and gene while preserving codon counts; projection must vanish.
Reject if SerSplit projection is carried by one gene, one assay, or one codon substitution direction.
data_sources: MaveDB and ProteinGym synonymous variant tables: variant sequence, reference codon, alternate codon, score, raw counts, replicate ID, assay type, selection condition
gene/transcript annotation for each MAVE library: CDS position, amino acid, codon context, expression construct, library design
matched codon-pair, RNA-structure, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-profiling controls for each assayed gene where available
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if MAVE coverage does not span all 61 codons, if effects are dominated by mRNA stability/codon-pair/dwell terms, if synonymous scores are too assay-specific, or if the model cannot identify codon effects separately from gene and position effects.
candidate_axes.name: synonymous_MAVE_effect_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT separately to each lesion chemistry and to any preregistered combined lesion axis. Report whether projection survives explicit GC and nearest-neighbor residualization.
candidate_axes.construction: Synthesize oligos in which only the central codon varies across the 61 sense codons and all flanking bases, concentration, exposure, time, temperature, and buffer are identical. For each damage chemistry, estimate lesion rate per molecule from raw replicate counts. Within chemistry and replicate batch, z-score lesion rates; aggregate independent chemistries only if preregistered or keep separate axes. The raw codon lesion vector x is then residualized against C plus explicit base-composition, purine/pyrimidine, CpG/UpA, and nearest-neighbor thermodynamic controls; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: No tRNA, codon usage, mRNA stability, codon-pair, ribosome, or expression data enter the raw axis.
Identical flanking contexts remove codon-pair and local transcript-context effects at the experimental design stage.
GC, nearest-neighbor chemistry, CpG/UpA, and base-position composition are residualized.
Run DNA-only and RNA-only panels separately; projection must not depend on a single chemistry unless that chemistry was preregistered.
Negative control: replicate the panel with scrambled codon labels before analysis; projection must vanish.
data_sources: bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic DNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon
bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic RNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon
LC-MS, primer-extension, nanopore, or sequencing readouts for UV dimerization, oxidative lesions, hydrolytic deamination, and alkylation under fixed exposure conditions
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if lesion-rate differences are fully explained by GC/base composition or nearest-neighbor chemistry, if replicate variance is too high, if synthesis bias differs by codon, or if no residual projection onto u_SerSplit remains.
candidate_axes.name: matched_trinucleotide_chemical_lesion_residual_axis

data_requests: Locked 61-sense-codon order used by codon_q6_selection_vectors.v1, with RNA codon spelling convention fixed as U/C/A/G.

Existing 64-row selection-vector packet and a 61-row sense-only extract with amino_acid, codon, is_sense, q6_bits, q6_label, d_perp_loading, f3_loading, optimal_loading, trna_consensus_loading, trna_supply_tai_centered_loading, and trna_supply_tai_mean.

Forbidden-control table C_base for the same 61 codons: intercept, 20 amino-acid one-hot columns, GC1, GC2, GC3, total_GC, CpG, UpA, purine/pyrimidine position indicators, wobble class, codon-family degeneracy, and any local graph covariates already used in the Window6--Codon-Q6 bridge.

Codon-pair control table: for each codon, incoming codon-pair residual score, outgoing codon-pair residual score, source organism, transcript set, normalization method, and whether stop-adjacent pairs were excluded.

mRNA-stability control table: per-codon matched-context predicted deltaG or stability contribution, source transcriptome, window size, folding software/version, expression weighting, and GC-controlled residual.

ribosome-dwell control table: per-codon dwell or pause residual from matched ribosome-profiling sources, source organism, protocol, footprint length handling, A/P/E-site assignment, expression threshold, and existing tRNA/GC/stability residualization status.

For tRNA-modification route: MODOMICS/GtRNAdb/tRNADB-CE joined table with organism, tRNA ID, isotype, anticodon, decoded codon set, mature sequence, modification position, modification identity, enzyme, evidence, and abundance/gene-copy columns marked as controls only.

For aaRS route: machine-readable kinetic table with organism, aaRS identity, tRNA substrate ID, anticodon, decoded codon, amino acid, kcat, Km, kcat/Km, replicate, temperature, pH, buffer, assay method, mutation status, and literature source.

For EF-Tu/EF1A route: binding table with organism, elongation factor, charged tRNA substrate ID, amino acid, anticodon, decoded codon, Kd or deltaG, kon, koff if available, buffer, temperature, replicate, modification state, and source.

For alternative-code route: codon reassignment event table with codon, standard assignment, observed assignment, taxon/clade, genome IDs, evidence type, confidence, inferred mechanism, GC content, codon disappearance score, tRNA-loss annotation, and phylogenetic deduplication ID.

For DNA mutability route: codon opportunity table, coding SNV table, de novo mutation table, methylation/CpG flags, local trinucleotide context, callable bases, transcript annotation, and filters for splice/regulatory overlap.

For RNA editing and mRNA modification routes: CDS-mapped event calls with transcript, coordinate, codon, codon position, event type, confidence, coverage, expression, tissue/cell type, platform, known DNA-variant exclusion, local motif, and mRNA half-life control.

For MAVE route: synonymous variant score table with raw counts, normalized scores, replicate IDs, reference codon, alternate codon, amino acid, gene, protein position, assay type, library design, and RNA/codon-context annotations.

For synthetic lesion route: raw replicate count matrix for 61 matched-flank DNA/RNA oligos, synthesis QC, concentration, exposure condition, chemistry, readout method, batch, and codon label key stored separately until after QC.
tests: TEST_AXIS_ADMISSIBILITY: For each candidate raw vector x, require one finite numeric value for every one of the 61 standard-code sense codons in the locked order. Missing codons, imputed codons not declared before testing, or post-hoc source changes make the candidate inadmissible.

TEST_FORBIDDEN_MATRIX: Build C from intercept, amino-acid one-hot, d_perp_loading, f3_loading, optimal_loading, trna_consensus_loading, trna_supply_tai_centered_loading, GC1, GC2, GC3, total_GC, CpG, UpA, wobble class, codon-family degeneracy, codon-pair incoming/outgoing residuals, mRNA-stability score, ribosome-dwell score, and any candidate-specific nuisance columns. Center and scale non-binary columns; drop linearly dependent columns by QR with locked tolerance 1e-10; set P_C=C(C^T C)^+C^T.

TEST_RESIDUALIZATION: For each x, compute r=(I-P_C)x. Reject if ||r||_2 <= 1e-12 or if any forbidden covariate predicts r in leave-one-source cross-validation with adjusted R2 >= 0.05. Define d_resid4=r/||r||_2 only after this rejection check is passed.

TEST_U_SERSPLIT: Let S4={UCU,UCC,UCA,UCG} and S2={AGU,AGC}. Define u_i=1/sqrt(12) for codons in S4, u_i=-2/sqrt(12) for codons in S2, and u_i=0 otherwise, in the locked 61-codon order. Compute u_r=(I-P_C)u. If ||u_r||_2 <= 1e-12, the SerSplit projection is not testable under the chosen controls. Otherwise define v=u_r/||u_r||_2 and rho=<d_resid4,v>; rho_abs=abs(rho).

TEST_WITHIN_SER_EXACT_NULL: Enumerate all 15 partitions of the six Ser codons into A of size 4 and B of size 2. For each partition define u_A,B with +1/sqrt(12) on A and -2/sqrt(12) on B, residualize by (I-P_C), discard zero residual contrasts, normalize, and compute T_A,B=abs(<d_resid4,v_A,B>). The exact within-Ser p-value is (number of retained partitions with T_A,B >= rho_abs)/(number of retained partitions).

TEST_SIXFOLD_FAMILY_EXACT_NULL: Enumerate every 4-versus-2 partition within each six-codon amino-acid family Ser, Leu, and Arg. Residualize, normalize, and compute absolute projections as above. The exact sixfold-family p-value is the fraction of retained contrasts with projection >= rho_abs. This tests whether the natural Ser split is exceptional relative to same-degeneracy amino-acid families, not whether it is biologically true.

TEST_GLOBAL_MATCHED_SUPPORT_NULL: Enumerate or Monte Carlo preregister all disjoint codon sets A,B with |A|=4 and |B|=2 that match the SerSplit contrast on total GC count and wobble-class counts; form the same zero-sum normalized contrast, residualize against C, normalize, and compare absolute projections to rho_abs. If exact enumeration exceeds the locked compute budget, use a stored seed and at least 1000000 matched draws, reported as an approximation rather than exact.

TEST_MULTIPLE_CANDIDATE_CONTROL: Because candidate_axes are generators, apply Holm correction to projection p-values across all admitted axes and all preregistered subaxes. Passing this test is a flag for further audit, not a scientific verdict.

TEST_NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: For each admitted axis, run the route-specific label, position, source, shifted-frame, or pseudo-codon negative controls. A candidate is rejected if any negative control gives a SerSplit projection with the same sign and at least 80% of rho_abs.

TEST_REPRODUCIBILITY: Split each data source by organism, clade, tissue, assay, platform, or batch as applicable. Reconstruct x, r, d_resid4, and rho in each split. Reject if the material projection is caused by one split or if sign is unstable after the sign convention is locked on the training split.

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residualized axis. Report rho, abs(rho), within-Ser exact p, sixfold-family exact p, global matched-support p, residual norm, and independence diagnostics. Treat any pass only as a candidate-axis flag, not as a scientific verdict.
oracle_json.construction: Restrict to mature tRNA features outside anticodon bases 34,35,36 and outside any annotation explicitly tied to wobble decoding. Encode positions 32,37,38 and non-anticodon body positions as binary modification presence, chemistry-class burden, enzyme-family burden, and evidence-weighted modification burden. Within each organism, z-score feature columns across tRNA isodecoders. Map each tRNA to directly cognate standard-code codons using the locked codon table. Aggregate multiple isodecoders per codon by median, then aggregate organisms by median or random-effects mean to obtain a finite 61-vector x. Residualize x against the forbidden-control matrix C containing intercept, amino-acid one-hot, tRNA supply/tAI, tRNA consensus loading, f3/ramp, d_perp, optimal loading, GC1, GC2, GC3, total GC, CpG, UpA, wobble class, codon-pair incoming/outgoing scores, mRNA-stability score, and ribosome-dwell score. If r=(I-P_C)x is nonzero, define d_resid4=r/||r||_2.
controls: Exclude anticodon-position and wobble-decoding modification features before construction, not merely after regression.
Use tRNA abundance, tAI, gene copy, and consensus loading only as forbidden controls, never as raw-axis inputs.
Reject if the residual axis is predictable from tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble, codon-pair effects, mRNA stability, or ribosome dwell with held-out adjusted R2 >= 0.05.
Run leave-one-organism, leave-one-clade, and leave-one-enzyme-family audits.
Negative controls: permute modification positions within tRNA bodies and permute anticodon labels within isotype; both must lose the u_SerSplit projection.
data_sources: MODOMICS tRNA modification records: organism, tRNA isotype, anticodon, mature-position number, modification identity, enzyme, evidence type
GtRNAdb 2.0 or tRNADB-CE tRNA gene/isodecoder records: organism, tRNA ID, isotype, anticodon, predicted mature sequence, decoded codon set
locked standard-code 61-sense-codon table from codon_q6_selection_vectors.v1
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if Ser UCN or AGY coverage is sparse, if the residual norm is near zero after forbidden controls, if the projection is driven by anticodon/wobble annotations or tRNA abundance, or if leave-one-source audits make the projection unstable.
oracle_json.name: non_wobble_tRNA_body_modification_residual_axis

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual kinetic axis. Also split public-only versus fill-in-only, and lock the sign convention on one split before checking the other.
oracle_json.construction: Use only wild-type, full-length, cognate aminoacylation assays. Exclude anticodon mutants, minihelix-only assays, noncognate mischarging assays, abundance proxies, and assays lacking codon-resolvable tRNA assignment. Convert kcat/Km to log10 units. Within each organism-aaRS-assay-method block, subtract the amino-acid-specific median and divide by MAD. Map each tRNA substrate to directly decoded standard codon(s); if a tRNA decodes multiple synonymous codons, assign only when the decoding set is preregistered and codon-resolvable, otherwise mark missing. Aggregate replicates by inverse-variance weighted mean, isodecoders by median, and organisms by random-effects mean to obtain x over 61 codons. Residualize x against C and set d_resid4=(I-P_C)x/||(I-P_C)x||_2 if admissible.
controls: Amino-acid one-hot columns in C remove amino-acid-level effects, including any Ser-level charging effect.
Anticodon-mutant and wobble-engineering assays are excluded from x.
Assay batch, organism, temperature, pH, and method are normalized before codon aggregation.
tRNA supply/tAI, tRNA consensus, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-dwell controls are residualized after aggregation.
Coverage gate: every sense codon must have direct or preregistered fill-in kinetic support; post-hoc imputation is not allowed.
data_sources: BRENDA and SABIO-RK aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase kinetic records: enzyme, organism, tRNA substrate, amino acid, kcat, Km, kcat/Km, temperature, pH, buffer, assay method
primary-literature extraction table for wild-type full-length cognate tRNA aminoacylation assays
bounded fill-in kinetic panel if public coverage is incomplete: at least one directly assigned mature cognate tRNA substrate for each of the 61 sense codons
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if fewer than 61 codons have direct kinetic support, if Ser codon values are inferred only from anticodon or wobble identity, if organism/method effects dominate, or if amino-acid and tRNA controls remove the residual projection.
oracle_json.name: aaRS_charging_kinetics_residual_axis

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the EF-Tu/EF1A residual axis. Require the same nonzero sign in at least two independent assay sources, or in one public source and the bounded fill-in panel, before flagging the route for further audit.
oracle_json.construction: For each charged full-length tRNA substrate, compute deltaG=RT ln(Kd) when Kd is available, or use reported deltaG. Exclude uncharged tRNAs, minihelices, anticodon mutants, noncognate substrates, and wobble-engineered constructs. Within each organism-factor-assay block, subtract the amino-acid median to remove amino-acid-side-chain binding compensation. Map charged tRNAs to directly cognate codons; aggregate replicates, isodecoders, and organisms using robust medians or random-effects means to form x. Residualize x against C and normalize the residual as d_resid4.
controls: Raw input is charged-tRNA binding thermodynamics, not tRNA supply, codon usage, mRNA stability, codon-pair effects, or ribosome dwell.
Amino-acid one-hot, tRNA supply/tAI, tRNA consensus, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble class, codon-pair scores, mRNA-stability score, and ribosome-dwell score are forbidden controls.
Reject if residualized binding values remain predictable from tRNA supply or wobble class.
Run buffer, organism, factor, and method leave-one-out audits.
Negative control: uncharged-tRNA binding, where available, must not reproduce the same SerSplit projection.
data_sources: published EF-Tu or EF1A charged-tRNA binding datasets with Kd, kon, koff, or deltaG for full-length aminoacyl-tRNAs
substrate metadata: organism, tRNA ID, anticodon, decoded codon set, amino acid, modification state, charging state, assay buffer, temperature
bounded 61-codon fill-in binding panel using matched charged mature tRNAs and one elongation-factor preparation
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if 61-codon charged-tRNA coverage cannot be obtained, if values are not codon-resolvable, if residuals are collinear with tRNA consensus or wobble class, or if the projection is batch-specific.
oracle_json.name: EF_Tu_EF1A_charged_tRNA_binding_residual_axis

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual error-susceptibility axis. Report projections separately for basal-condition reporters and any stress-condition subaxis, with multiple-test correction.
oracle_json.construction: Use only assays where the variable feature is the target sense codon in a matched reporter context. Estimate logit(error_rate) or log(error_rate per translated codon) with binomial or count uncertainty. Exclude assays measuring elongation speed, pause duration, ribosome dwell, codon-pair effects, or stress-induced global translational shutdown. Within each assay and organism, center by amino-acid median and normalize by replicate uncertainty. Aggregate matched-context codon effects to a 61-vector x. Residualize x against C plus near-cognate Hamming-neighborhood composition columns and normalize the residual to d_resid4.
controls: The route targets codon-resolved decoding error susceptibility, explicitly excluding ribosome dwell or pause duration as raw inputs.
Identical reporter flanks remove codon-pair and local mRNA-stability variation at the design stage for bounded panels.
Amino-acid, tRNA supply/tAI, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble class, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-dwell controls are included in C.
Exclude antibiotic or stress conditions unless analyzed as separate preregistered subaxes.
Negative controls: swap reporter flanking contexts and permute codon labels within amino acid; the u_SerSplit projection must not persist.
data_sources: dual-luciferase, fluorescence, mass-spectrometry, or deep-mutational reporter assays measuring synonymous codon-specific mistranslation or near-cognate error rates
bounded 61-codon matched reporter panel: identical transcript, identical flanking codons, single variable A-site codon, matched expression construct
metadata: organism, strain, reporter sequence, target codon, measured error rate, read depth, replicate, antibiotic/stress condition, growth condition
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if codon-specific error rates are explained by wobble, tRNA supply, near-cognate neighborhood, or ribosome dwell; if matched 61-codon coverage is unavailable; or if the projection appears only in one reporter construct.
oracle_json.name: decoding_error_susceptibility_residual_axis

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the lability residual axis. Report whether rho survives the exclusion of events annotated as tRNA-loss-driven, wobble-driven, GC-driven, codon-disappearance-driven, or stop-adjacent.
oracle_json.construction: For each standard-code sense codon, count phylogenetically deduplicated independent events in which that codon changes amino-acid meaning or becomes stop in an alternative code. Exclude events whose only annotated support is tRNA abundance loss, codon disappearance, wobble expansion, GC shift, or ambiguous low-confidence inference. Compute x_i=log((events_i+0.5)/(opportunities_i-events_i+0.5)), where opportunities_i is the number of screened independent clades in which codon i is observable and assessable. Residualize x against C plus codon-family degeneracy and stop-adjacency indicators. Normalize the residual to d_resid4 if admissible.
controls: Phylogenetic deduplication prevents a single clade expansion from counting as multiple events.
tRNA supply loss, wobble expansion, GC shift, codon disappearance, codon-pair effects, mRNA stability, and ribosome dwell are exclusion reasons or forbidden controls, not explanatory inputs.
Remove all stop codons from the 61-vector; stop-adjacency enters only as a nuisance control.
Repeat after excluding mitochondrial codes and after excluding bacterial/archaeal candidate recodings.
Negative control: randomize reassignment events across codons within matched degeneracy and GC classes.
data_sources: NCBI Genetic Codes table snapshot: code ID, taxon scope, codon assignment, evidence note
Codetta or equivalent genome-scale alternative-code screen calls: genome ID, codon reassignment, confidence, clade, inferred mechanism if annotated
GTDB or NCBI taxonomy tree for phylogenetic deduplication of reassignment events
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if reassignment counts are too sparse, if SerSplit is explained by tRNA supply or wobble mechanisms, if stop-adjacent artifacts dominate, or if residualization collapses the axis.
oracle_json.name: codon_assignment_lability_residual_axis

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual DNA mutability axis. Also report rho after removing CpG-containing codons and after matching UCN and AGY codons by callable opportunity where feasible.
oracle_json.construction: For each sense codon, compute opportunity-normalized rare synonymous SNV burden from that reference codon per callable occurrence. Stratify by strand, methylated-CpG status, local trinucleotide context, replication timing, expression, and gene constraint. Use only variants classified as synonymous in the locked transcript set. Exclude variants affecting splice motifs, overlapping regulatory elements, RNA-editing sites, or disease-enriched regions. Fit an expected neutral-context model from noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites, subtract expected burden, and aggregate the codon residuals into x. Residualize x against C plus CpG/UpA and local trinucleotide mutability columns; normalize to d_resid4.
controls: Raw axis is DNA mutability or repair residual, not translation efficiency, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, codon-pair effects, mRNA stability, or ribosome dwell.
GC1, GC2, GC3, total GC, CpG, UpA, methylation, trinucleotide opportunity, codon-pair scores, mRNA-stability scores, and dwell scores are controls.

Negative control: frame-shifted intronic pseudo-codons from the same genes must not reproduce the projection.
data_sources: gnomAD or comparable rare synonymous coding SNV table: variant, allele count, allele number, gene, transcript, codon, ancestral/ref/alt allele, consequence
large de novo mutation table with callable opportunity mask
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon coordinate, reading frame, exon, strand
methylation, replication timing, trinucleotide mutability, and local repair covariate tracks
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if GC, CpG, trinucleotide context, methylation, callability, or coding selection explains the residual; if the 61-codon opportunity table is incomplete; or if de novo-only data do not support the same directional projection.

controls: DNA SNPs, mapping artifacts, and low-coverage calls are excluded.

GTEx, ENCODE, or matched RNA-seq coverage/expression table for opportunity normalization
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation with codon coordinate and reading frame
known DNA variant databases for excluding genomic polymorphisms

Normalize within study by expression, coverage, calling platform, local motif score, local structure, and modification-specific callable-base opportunity. Run platform-specific audits for antibody-based, chemical-mapping, and direct-RNA/nanopore calls where available.

GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon coordinate, reading frame
matched expression, mRNA half-life, local motif, local structure, and RBP-density tracks

Run leave-one-gene, leave-one-assay-type, and leave-one-library audits.

library metadata: gene, transcript, CDS position, amino acid, local codon context, construct design, expression system
matched RNA-structure, mRNA-stability, codon-pair, expression, and ribosome-profiling controls where available
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if public MAVE coverage does not span all 61 codons, if codon effects are not identifiable separately from gene/position/context effects, or if forbidden controls remove the residual projection.

LC-MS, primer-extension, nanopore, or sequencing readouts for UV dimerization, oxidative lesions, hydrolytic deamination, and alkylation under fixed exposure conditions

oracle_response:
Candidate-only boundary: I would treat every route below as a generator of an auditable 61-codon vector, not as evidence that the Stop/Ser graph defect is biologically certified. A route only becomes admissible after it produces a finite value for every standard-code sense codon and after the raw vector is residualized against the full forbidden block.
Common admissibility contract
Let the codon order be the locked 61-row sense-only order from codon_q6_selection_vectors.v1. For any proposed raw codon vector  $x\in\mathbb{R}^{61}$ , build a forbidden-control matrix  $C$  with:

$$C=[1,\ \text{amino-acid one-hot},\ d_\perp,\ f3/ramp,\ \text{optimal},\ \text{tRNA consensus},\ \text{tRNA supply/tAI},\ GC_1,GC_2,GC_3,GC_{\rm total},\ CpG,\ UpA,\ \text{wobble class},\ \text{codon-pair in/out},\ \text{mRNA stability},\ \text{ribosome dwell},\ \text{route-specific nuisance columns}]$$

Do not use the local edge-defect decomposition, q6_label, q6_bits, Stop codons, or  $u_{\rm SerSplit}$  to construct  $x$ . They can appear only in post-hoc audit reports or optional robustness controls, not in the raw axis factory.
Drop linearly dependent columns in  $C$  by QR/SVD with a locked tolerance, for example  $10^{-10}$ . Define

$$P_C=C(C^\top C)^+C^\top,\quad r_x=(I-P_C)x.$$

The route fails if  $\|r_x\|_2\le 10^{-12}$ . Otherwise,

$$d_{\rm resid4}=\frac{r_x}{\|r_x\|_2}.$$

A stricter independence gate should also be applied: the residual must not be predictably reconstructible from any forbidden block by leave-one-source, leave-one-clade, or leave-one-assay cross-validation. A practical rejection rule is adjusted  $R^2\ge 0.05$  for any forbidden block or for the joint forbidden block after permutation calibration.
Exact projection test for  $u_{\rm SerSplit}$ 
Define the Ser split contrast on the 61 sense codons:

$$S_4=\{UCU,UCC,UCA,UCG\},\quad S_2=\{AGU,AGC\}.$$


$$u_i=
\begin{cases}
1/\sqrt{12}, & i\in S_4\\
-2/\sqrt{12}, & i\in S_2\\
0, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}$$

Residualize the contrast through the same forbidden matrix:

$$u_r=(I-P_C)u.$$

If  $\|u_r\|_2\le 10^{-12}$ , the SerSplit projection is not testable under that control set. Otherwise define

$$v_{\rm SerSplit}=u_r/\|u_r\|_2,\quad \rho=\langle d_{\rm resid4},v_{\rm SerSplit}\rangle,\quad T_{\rm obs}=|\rho|.$$

Use exact nulls rather than asymptotics:


Within-Ser exact null. Enumerate all  $\binom{6}{4}=15$  partitions of the six Ser codons into a 4-set  $A$  and 2-set  $B$ . For each, construct the same zero-sum contrast, residualize by  $I-P_C$ , normalize if nonzero, and compute  $T_j=|\langle d_{\rm resid4},v_j\rangle|$ . The exact p-value is the retained fraction with  $T_j\ge T_{\rm obs}$ .


Sixfold-family exact null. Repeat the same 4-versus-2 enumeration for Ser, Leu, and Arg, the three six-codon amino-acid families. This tests whether the Ser partition is exceptional relative to same-degeneracy families.


Global matched-support null. Enumerate, or preregister a seeded Monte Carlo draw of at least  $10^6$  contrasts, over disjoint codon sets  $A,B$  with  $|A|=4,|B|=2$ , matched to the Ser contrast on total GC, position-wise GC, wobble-class counts, and degeneracy class where feasible. Residualize and compare absolute projections.


A route “passes” only as a candidate-axis flag: finite axis constructed, forbidden-block residual nonzero, independence audits passed, exact projection detected. It still does not certify the graph-theoretic defect biologically.

Strongest candidate routes
1. Matched-flank chemical lesion residual axis
This is the cleanest non-translation route because the raw signal can be generated without tRNAs, ribosomes, codon usage, transcript abundance, or protein selection.
Finite data source. Synthesize a 61-oligo DNA panel and a 61-oligo RNA panel. Each oligo has identical flanking sequence and differs only in the central sense codon. Run fixed-condition chemical lesion assays: UV dimerization, oxidative damage, alkylation, deamination, and optionally ribose/backbone cleavage for RNA.
Required fields. Codon, full oligo sequence, DNA/RNA flag, chemistry, exposure dose, time, buffer, temperature, molecule count, lesion count, readout method, replicate, batch, synthesis QC, purity, barcode, and blinded codon-label key.
Construction. For each chemistry, estimate a lesion rate or hazard:

$$x_{i,c}=\log\frac{\text{lesion}_{i,c}+1/2}{\text{molecules}_{i,c}+1}.$$

Normalize within chemistry and batch by z-score or batch random effect. Aggregate preregistered chemistries either separately or by inverse-variance mean. Residualize against  $C$  plus nearest-neighbor thermodynamic terms, CpG/UpA, purine/pyrimidine position indicators, and synthesis-QC covariates.
Why it is not explained by forbidden axes. The raw measurement has no tRNA supply, no f3/ramp, no codon-pair context beyond identical flanks, no mRNA stability model, and no ribosome dwell. GC and nearest-neighbor chemistry are explicitly residualized.
Exclusion controls. Reject oligos with failed synthesis QC. Keep codon labels blinded until rates are frozen. Run scrambled-label negative controls. Repeat with at least two flank backgrounds to test whether any projection is flank-specific.
Failure mode. Most of the signal may be base composition or nearest-neighbor chemistry. If residualization removes the vector, the route fails cleanly.
Why this is high value. It gives a codon-level residual axis that is physically real but translation-independent. If it projects onto SerSplit, it is not a tRNA-supply or ribosome-dwell artifact; if it fails, the audit is still decisive.

2. Synonymous DNA damage/repair/mutability residual axis
This route uses natural genetic variation but aims to isolate codon-level mutability rather than selection or translation. gnomAD v4 is large enough to support rare-variant codon opportunity calculations; its v4 release reported 807,162 total individuals, split into exome and genome callsets aligned to GRCh38. GENCODE provides current human/mouse annotation releases and states its goal as identifying and classifying gene features with high accuracy based on biological evidence. gnomAD+1
Finite data sources. gnomAD rare synonymous SNVs, a de novo mutation catalog with callable masks, GENCODE or RefSeq CDS annotations, methylation/CpG tracks, replication timing, trinucleotide mutability model, local callability, and gene constraint annotations.
Required fields. Codon, transcript ID, CDS coordinate, reference codon, alternate codon, synonymous consequence, allele count, allele number, callable opportunity, strand, local trinucleotide, methylation flag, replication timing, expression/callability, gene constraint, splice distance, regulatory-overlap flag.
Construction. Count rare synonymous SNVs by reference codon per callable codon occurrence. Fit an expected neutral mutation model using noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites:

$$E[\text{SNV}]\sim \text{trinucleotide}+\text{methylation}+\text{strand}+\text{replication timing}+\text{callability}+\text{gene constraint}.$$

For each codon, compute a standardized residual burden:

$$x_i=\frac{O_i-E_i}{\sqrt{E_i+\epsilon}}.$$

Residualize  $x$  against  $C$  plus CpG, UpA, trinucleotide opportunity, and methylation.
Why it is not explained by forbidden axes. The raw mechanism is DNA mutability/repair, not translation efficiency. tRNA supply, f3/ramp,  $d_\perp$ , wobble, codon-pair, mRNA stability, and ribosome dwell enter only as forbidden controls.
Exclusion controls. Exclude splice-proximal, disease-enriched, low-callability, overlapping regulatory, RNA-editing, and repetitive regions. Repeat using de novo-only mutations. Repeat after removing CpG-containing codons.
Failure mode. If GC/trinucleotide/CpG explains everything, the residual vanishes. If de novo-only data do not agree directionally with population rare variants, treat the axis as likely selection- or ascertainment-contaminated.

3. Coding RNA editing and mRNA base-modification residual axis
This is a transcript-chemistry route. It is more biological than the synthetic lesion axis but still not a tRNA-supply, ramp, or dwell axis if handled carefully. RMBase v3.0 describes itself as integrating large epitranscriptome sequencing data and reports 73 RNA modification types across 62 species and 1,074,100 modification sites; RMBase v2 also documents modification-site, motif, RBP, and SNV-related modules. RNA Lab+1
Finite data sources. RMBase v3, m6A-Atlas/DirectRMDB if available, REDIportal/RADAR-style RNA-editing calls, GENCODE CDS annotation, matched RNA-seq coverage, tissue expression, mRNA half-life, local RNA structure, motif scores, RBP-density tracks, known DNA-variant masks.
Required fields. Transcript ID, genome coordinate, CDS coordinate, codon, codon position, modification/editing type, editing or modification level, coverage, confidence, tissue/cell type, platform, expression, local motif, strand, DNA-variant exclusion status, mRNA half-life, predicted local structure.
Construction. Map high-confidence CDS events to codon identity. For each codon, compute an opportunity-normalized event burden:

$$x_i=\operatorname{median}_{tissue,platform}\left[
\log\frac{\text{events}_{i}+1/2}{\text{callable expressed codon opportunities}_{i}+1}
\right].$$

Build separate raw axes for A-to-I editing, C-to-U editing, m6A, m5C, pseudouridine, and a preregistered combined modification burden. Normalize within tissue/platform before codon aggregation. Residualize against  $C$  plus expression, editable-base opportunity, local motif, mRNA half-life, local structure, and RBP density.
Why it is not explained by forbidden axes. It measures editing/modification propensity after controlling expression, motifs, stability, and structure. mRNA stability is a nuisance column, not the axis.
Exclusion controls. Remove known genomic SNPs, low-read-depth calls, mapping-ambiguous sites, repetitive regions, and sites not confidently in CDS. Run +1 and +2 shifted reading-frame pseudo-codon controls. Run tissue leave-one-out and platform leave-one-out audits.
Failure mode. Very likely confounded by base motif and transcript structure. If the SerSplit projection survives only one tissue, one platform, or one modification caller, reject.

4. Genetic-code reassignment/lability residual axis
This route asks whether a standard-code sense codon has independently changed assignment across known or screened genetic codes after removing GC, codon disappearance, tRNA-loss, and wobble mechanisms. NCBI’s genetic-code table lists the standard code and alternative codes, gives a last-update date of September 23, 2024, and explains that its displayed tables use T rather than U for GenBank convention. ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
Finite data sources. NCBI Genetic Codes, Codetta or equivalent alternative-code genome screens, GTDB/NCBI taxonomy, genome-level codon-usage and GC summaries, tRNA-loss/wobble/codon-disappearance annotations where available.
Required fields. The strongest mechanism is codon-specific translational fidelity under serine-charging stress: UCN and AGY are not merely two spellings for Ser; they can behave as two discrete Ser decoding channels whose failure modes differ. The pressure would not be “use the abundant tRNA,” “avoid slow codons,” or “optimize GC.” It would be: at highly translated Ser sites, choose the Ser codon island whose charged-tRNA competition and near-cognate error spectrum produce the lowest cost of wrong protein products under the relevant cellular state.
The reason this is the strongest route is that it touches the Hamming-1 defect directly. A Hamming-1 synonymous edge hides a one-base decoding or mutation error: the wrong triplet still gives the same amino acid. The Ser split removes that local safety path between UCN and AGY. The UCN island and AGY island therefore expose different one-step error neighborhoods. UCN Ser codons are surrounded by one set of possible missense/nonsense outcomes; AGY Ser codons are surrounded by another. Translation errors are real at biologically relevant rates, with estimates commonly in the range of roughly  $10^{-5}$  to  $10^{-3}$  misincorporated amino acids per codon depending on system and conditions, and can arise either from wrong codon–tRNA pairing or from wrong aminoacylation. 维基百科
The mechanistic route would be this: SerRS charges multiple Ser tRNA isoacceptors, and UCN versus AGY codons are decoded through different Ser-tRNA channels. Under normal growth, those channels may look mostly redundant. Under serine limitation, one-carbon/metabolic stress, oxidative stress, altered SerRS activity, or tRNA-modification stress, the degeneracy can be lifted: one Ser codon island remains robustly translated while the other becomes error-prone, undercharged, or prone to a different near-cognate substitution spectrum. This kind of “degeneracy lifting” is not fanciful: a synthetic-reporter study in E. coli found that amino-acid perturbations can split synonymous codons into robust and sensitive classes, with protein-synthesis differences up to orders of magnitude, and reported that the hierarchy was not explained by usual tRNA abundance or codon-usage rules but by competition among tRNA isoacceptors for aminoacylation. arXiv Serine–tRNA ligase is exactly the enzyme class that converts serine plus tRNA into seryl-tRNA, so this route acts before ribosomal dwell and before ordinary codon-speed explanations. 维基百科
The biological pressure would therefore be error-cost minimization at Ser positions, not speed optimization. A UCN→AGY synonymous replacement would keep the amino acid fixed but would switch the residue into a different biochemical decoding channel and a different near-cognate error shell. In a highly expressed protein, even a small increase in Ser→Arg, Ser→Gly, Ser→Cys, Ser→Thr, Ser→Stop, or other mistranslation products could matter if the Ser site is catalytic, phosphorylated, structurally buried, aggregation-prone, or near an interaction surface. The standard-code fact that Ser is encoded by UCN and AGY is captured in the standard genetic-code table; NCBI’s standard translation table encodes the split in its Ser positions, while alternative mitochondrial codes also show that the AGN/Ser/Arg boundary is evolutionarily labile in some systems, which is suggestive but not by itself evidence for this mechanism. 国家生物技术信息中心 国家生物技术信息中心
The decisive confounders are severe. First, this must not collapse into charged tRNA supply; if aminoacylated Ser-tRNA abundance alone explains the effect, the mechanism is just supply under another name. The surviving signal has to be kinetic or fidelity-like: same mature tRNA abundance, same codon context, but different charging robustness or wrong-amino-acid spectrum. Second, it must not be wobble; any effect explainable by anticodon position, wobble modification, or decoding breadth is disqualified. Third, it must survive controls for GC, codon-pair context, local RNA structure/stability, and ribosome dwell, because UCN and AGY differ strongly in sequence composition. Fourth, it must not be a protein-biology artifact: Ser codon usage could correlate with phosphorylation motifs, disorder, low-complexity regions, catalytic Ser, secretion, or organism-specific gene classes without being a translation-selection axis. Fifth, it must separate protein yield from protein correctness. A dwell or initiation effect changes how much protein is made; this hypothesis predicts a codon-island-specific change in the identity and cost of erroneous products.
A clean surviving observation would look like this: in matched reporters or endogenous recoding experiments, UCN↔AGY swaps at the same Ser residue, with matched GC/codon-pair/RNA-structure/dwell and equal tRNA abundance, produce different aminoacylation robustness or different mistranslated peptide spectra under a relevant condition; the preferred island is the one whose measured error products are less damaging for that residue class. That would make the Ser split biologically meaningful without claiming that the graph defect itself is a certificate.
If this route survives, the sharpest next question is: Do highly expressed proteins preferentially place UCN versus AGY Ser codons at exactly those Ser residues where the opposite island’s measured near-cognate error spectrum would be more damaging?

The strongest mechanism is codon-island-specific translational fidelity selection: UCN-Ser and AGY-Ser are not merely two synonymous spellings; they expose a Ser residue to different one-error neighborhoods and different Ser-tRNA decoding channels. The relevant pressure would be minimizing the cost of incorrect protein products, not maximizing speed or matching abundant tRNAs.
The key point is that the Ser split is topologically special. Leu and Arg are also six-codon amino acids, but their 4+2 blocks are connected by Hamming-1 synonymous bridges. Ser is not: UCU/UCC/UCA/UCG and AGU/AGC form two disconnected synonymous islands. In the standard code, NCBI’s table encodes Ser in both the UCN block and the AGY block, with no one-base synonymous path between those blocks. 国家生物技术信息中心
Why this could matter biologically: a one-base translational misread, transcriptional error, or local decoding ambiguity around a UCN Ser codon samples a different set of wrong amino acids than the same kind of error around an AGY Ser codon. UCN Ser codons sit near Pro, Thr, Ala, Phe/Tyr/Cys, Leu/Trp, and for UCA/UCG even Stop-neighbor outcomes through second-position changes. AGY Ser codons sit near Cys, Arg, Gly, Asn, Thr, Ile, and Arg through third-position changes. So the Ser split could encode a choice between two error-cost spectra. A synonymous UCN→AGY replacement would preserve Ser in the intended translation product while changing the likely identities of mistranslated products.
The plausible molecular route is:
SerRS charges multiple Ser tRNA isoacceptors. UCN and AGY are decoded through different Ser-tRNA channels. Under ordinary conditions, these channels may be nearly equivalent. Under serine limitation, one-carbon/metabolic stress, oxidative stress, altered SerRS activity, tRNA-modification stress, or proteostasis pressure, the degeneracy can be lifted: one island may remain high-fidelity while the other becomes more prone to near-cognate acceptance, undercharging, mischarging, premature termination, or a different distribution of wrong amino-acid insertions. This is not a purely hypothetical class of phenomenon: Subramaniam, Pan, and Cluzel measured synthetic reporters in E. coli and found that amino-acid limitation can split synonymous codons into robust and sensitive classes, with up to roughly hundred-fold differences in protein synthesis; they reported that this hierarchy was not explained by ordinary tRNA abundance or codon usage, but by competition among tRNA isoacceptors for aminoacylation. arXiv
But for the present question, the strongest version is not “UCN has more charged tRNA than AGY.” That would be reducible to supply. The stronger version is: UCN and AGY have different conditional fidelity landscapes even after equalizing or controlling charged-tRNA availability. The axis is the identity and cost of erroneous products per Ser codon, not the amount of correctly charged tRNA or the dwell time of the ribosome. A UCN codon and an AGY codon at the same Ser residue could produce the same intended protein at similar abundance and speed, yet differ in the rare but costly products they generate. In highly expressed proteins, rare mistranslation events can become abundant enough for proteotoxic, dominant-negative, catalytic-site, phosphorylation-site, or aggregation costs to be selected.
This is the route that best aligns with the graph fact. A missing Hamming-1 synonymous bridge is exactly relevant when the biological pressure is about one-step errors. If the pressure were only tRNA supply, GC, codon-pair usage, mRNA folding, or ribosome speed, the graph defect would be mostly decorative. But if the pressure is which nonsynonymous errors are exposed around a Ser codon, then the disconnected Ser islands become mechanistically meaningful: they define two alternative local error neighborhoods for the same amino acid.
The decisive confounders are harsh.
First, charged-tRNA supply in disguise. If the effect disappears after controlling the concentration of aminoacylated Ser-tRNA isoacceptors, or if it is predicted by tAI/gene copy/charged fraction alone, then it is not the desired mechanism. The surviving signal must be a fidelity or error-spectrum difference at matched charged-tRNA availability.
Second, wobble in disguise. AGY and UCN necessarily involve different anticodon systems, and wobble modifications can dominate decoding behavior. A credible mechanism must show that the relevant difference is not simply position-34 pairing breadth or a known wobble modification. Ideally, the signal would involve first- or second-position near-cognate error spectra, SerRS/EF-Tu/tRNA-body effects, or wrong-product identities after wobble terms are controlled.
Third, speed masquerading as accuracy. A lower protein signal from one island under stress could be ribosome dwell, queuing, collision, premature drop-off, or global translational repression. The decisive readout is not fluorescence or ribosome occupancy; it is peptide-resolved mistranslation: what wrong amino acids appear at the Ser site, at what rate, and with what fitness/proteostasis cost.
Fourth, sequence-composition confounding. UCN and AGY differ strongly in bases, so GC, CpG/UpA, RNA structure, mRNA stability, codon-pair context, and local motifs can all fake an island effect. The same Ser residue must be tested in matched sequence contexts where these are held constant or explicitly neutralized.
Fifth, protein-position confounding. Natural UCN/AGY usage may correlate with phosphorylation motifs, disorder, low-complexity regions, catalytic Ser residues, secretion signals, transmembrane regions, splice enhancers, DNA methylation, or gene class. If AGY is enriched at a particular biological class of Ser sites, that does not prove translation-level selection. The mechanism survives only if synonymous recoding at the same Ser site changes the measured error spectrum or error cost.
Sixth, global stress physiology. Serine limitation and one-carbon stress alter metabolism, transcription, translation initiation, amino-acid pools, redox state, and proteostasis. A Ser-codon effect has to be separable from general stress response.
The cleanest surviving observation would be this: at the same Ser residue, in the same mRNA context, with matched expression, matched charged-tRNA availability, matched ribosome dwell, and matched RNA stability, UCN and AGY produce measurably different rare mistranslated peptide spectra; the naturally preferred codon island is the one whose wrong-product spectrum is less damaging at that residue class.
If this route survives, the sharpest next question is: Do highly expressed genes preferentially use UCN or AGY at exactly those Ser residues where the opposite island’s experimentally measured mistranslation spectrum would be more damaging?

Selection would act not on translation speed or average Ser incorporation, but on the expression-weighted damage caused by the small fraction of mistranslated protein molecules.
The mechanistic quantity is approximately

$$C(c,s,\sigma)=E_g\sum_{a\neq \mathrm{Ser}}p(a\mid c,\sigma)\,D_s(a),$$

where  $c$  is a Ser codon,  $s$  is the protein site,  $\sigma$  is the physiological state,  $E_g$  is the gene’s translation burden,  $p(a\mid c,\sigma)$  is the probability of inserting amino acid  $a$ , and  $D_s(a)$  is the site-specific cost of that substitution. UCN and AGY can then be viewed as two error palettes for the same intended residue.
That interpretation uses the graph structure directly. Ignoring third-position events, UCN codons have one-mismatch neighborhoods leading toward Pro, Thr, Ala and, depending on the third base, Phe, Leu, Tyr, Cys, Trp, or Stop. AGY instead points toward Cys, Arg, Gly, Ile, Thr, and Asn. Thus UCN↔AGY recoding can preserve the intended protein sequence while changing the identities of rare wrong products. Selection for robustness against mistranslation has long been proposed to strengthen with protein expression. arXiv

The cleanest first experiment is:
DMS-weighted mistranslation robustness of the standard genetic code.
Use ProteinGym as the primary public dataset. It is realistically fetchable: the official ProteinGym repository describes a substitution benchmark with roughly 2.7 million missense variants across 217 DMS assays, with processed files containing mutant, mutated_sequence, DMS_score, and binarized fitness columns; higher DMS_score is consistently higher fitness across assays. GitHub
The experiment should not test codon usage. It should test the genetic code map itself.
First construct a DMS-derived amino-acid damage matrix:

$$D(a\to b)=\operatorname{median}_{\text{assays},\,\text{sites with WT }a}
\left[
S_{\mathrm{WT}}-S_{a\to b}
\right],$$

where  $S$  is the normalized DMS score within each assay. Use only single amino-acid substitutions. Winsorize or rank-normalize scores within assay so one high-dynamic-range assay cannot dominate. If a pair  $a\to b$  is poorly covered, mark it missing and either drop all code-neighbor terms needing it or use a pre-registered shrinkage estimate toward the amino-acid-pair median. Do not use amino-acid physicochemical properties.

$$R(g)=
\frac{
\sum_{c\in \mathrm{sense}}
\sum_{c'\sim c}
w(c\to c')\,
L_g(c,c')
}{
\sum_{c\in \mathrm{sense}}
\sum_{c'\sim c}
w(c\to c')
},$$

where  $c'\sim c$  means Hamming-1 codon neighbor. For a neighbor that maps to the same amino acid, set

$$L_g(c,c')=0.$$

For a missense neighbor,

$$L_g(c,c')=D(g(c)\to g(c')).$$

For a stop neighbor, use a pre-registered large penalty estimated from nonsense DMS variants if available in the same assays, otherwise run the primary analysis on sense-to-sense neighbors only and report stop-neighbor robustness separately. The primary statistic should be sense-to-sense to avoid letting Stop dominate the answer.

The primary version is label-free uniform one-step error weight:

$$w=1.$$

The secondary version uses a fixed empirical mutation/misread weight by position and transition/transversion class, but this must be sensitivity analysis, not the primary result. Otherwise the test becomes about a chosen error model rather than about the graph fact.

$$T_{\mathrm{std}}=R(g_{\mathrm{std}}).$$

\text{all random genetic codes with the standard amino-acid/Stop degeneracy profile fixed}.$$

Amino-acid labels are fixed because the DMS matrix is label-specific. Codon assignments are randomized uniformly subject to those multiplicities. \Pr_{\Omega_{\mathrm{deg}}}

The standard code is not strongly exceptional under  $\Omega_{\mathrm{deg},e}$ .
